name: Capsaicin

lead: Capsaicin is the pungent compound in chili peppers, best known as the agent that produces heat and as the active ingredient in topical pain creams and pepper sprays. It is also sold in capsule form as a thermogenic and appetite supplement.

In small human studies it modestly raises energy expenditure and fat oxidation and may lower appetite. Meta-analyses of its effect on body weight show small or inconsistent benefits that are unlikely to be noticeable in body appearance.

paras: Capsaicin activates the TRPV1 ion channel on sensory neurons, triggering sympathetic nervous system activity and increased catecholamine release, which raises thermogenesis slightly. It may also affect satiety signalling and brown adipose tissue activity.

Oral use can cause stomach pain, burning, nausea and diarrhoea, and it may worsen reflux. Topical capsaicin causes burning and irritation, and contact with eyes or broken skin is painful. It is legal and unscheduled in food and supplement form.
